thread:
samir: starting canary for release r3.14 -> rolling 10% to canary now. watching latency and 5xx. will update.
amelia: noted, paging oncall if anything fires. I set a short-lived canary window of 15m.
deploy-bot: Deploy r3.14 initiating: service=redwood-api target=canary replicas=2 -> deployed
jordan: seeing a handful of alerts already: `http_5xx_rate` firing for canary slice. small numbers but spiky.
incident-bot: Paging on-call: @oncall, 5xx-rate threshold exceeded for redwood-api (canary). Incident id INC-2026-0423
oncall: on it. joining thread.
amelia: can folks paste the exact alert rule? curious if this is duped by throttling.
samir: alert is `sum(rate(http_server_errors[1m])) by (env) > 5` for canary env. Not ideal, comparing raw counts across tiny canary pool.
jordan: oh — the alert uses absolute >5, and our canary has 2 pods; any blip will trigger. that explains noisy firing.
nora: that's a bad signal for canary. we should have ratio-based alert for small pools. creating an issues/ops ticket after live.
amelia: agree. for now, do we want to continue canary? customers might see errors — support slack thread? samir, can you check if errors are 500 or 429?
samir: digging into logs. quick tail:
```
# kubectl -n prod logs -l deployment=redwood-api-canary --tail=200
ERROR 2026-04-23T15:02:12Z service request failed status=500 msg="nil pointer"
WARN  2026-04-23T15:02:13Z rate limiter triggered: client=svc-a status=429
ERROR 2026-04-23T15:02:14Z service request failed status=502 msg="upstream timeout"
```
jordan: mixed errors — 500/502 and some 429s. looks like canary pods getting a different traffic pattern? maybe a compatibility bug in model routing.
oncall: what's the customer impact? any user-facing degradation reported?
samir: internal monitoring shows ~3.8% of traffic to canary had >1s latency and 0.9% 5xx during last 5m. overall platform impact negligible so far, but could escalate.
amelia: policy: if customer-facing errors >1% or SLO burn visible on customer routes, kill flag / rollback. samir, can you flip the feature flag to kill canary traffic while we triage?
samir: initiating feature flag kill via LaunchDarkly: `ldClient.variation('canary-release-r3.14', false)`
deploy-bot: Feature flag kill requested by samir. Waiting for confirm.
samir: done. verified via `curl` to header `x-canary-alloc` shows nothing.
nora: still seeing alerts — because alert rule aggregates on env label not flag. need to silence alert or change selector.
jordan: I can mute the on-call pager for the rule for 30m — propose muting until we roll back.
oncall: muted `alert: http_5xx_rate` for 30m. adding note: muting due to noisy canary that uses absolute thresholds. INC-2026-0423 updated.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 status: mitigation-in-progress. responders: samir, amelia, jordan.
amelia: since flag kill didn't fully stop symptoms for ~2m, I'm going to start rollback to previous stable: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-api --to-revision=42`
samir: thumbs up, coordinating. will watch health checks.
deploy-bot: Rollback command executed by amelia. pods scaling down/up.
jordan: watching metrics — latency and 5xx dropping back toward baseline. good signal. i'll keep an eye for any cascading errors.
samir: quick postmortem notes while warm: root cause likely a model routing mismatch in r3.14 that hits an edge-case path leading to nil pointer on some requests. canary pool small + absolute alert caused immediate noise.
nora: observability gap: there is no dedicated canary dashboard for r3.* with percentage-based error rates and per-pod insights; on-call had to piece together logs + raw alerts.
amelia: agree — also alerting config uses absolute counts for error-rate threshold. for small canaries this should be rate per 1000 reqs or ratio.
oncall: customer impact summary: estimated <1% of live customers saw degraded responses during the 7m window before the flag kill; no escalations from support yet, monitoring ticket opened.
jordan: action items from live: 1) convert canary alerts to ratio-based or add minimum window, 2) create a canary dashboard template (per-release) in Grafana, 3) add a runbook step: prefer flag kill over immediate rollback if the issue is partial and kills more routes.
samir: adding to backlog and will PR for alert rule change: `expr = sum(rate(http_server_errors[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.01` with `min_request_threshold=100` for small pools.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 updated: mitigation=flag-kill+rollback, severity=sev2, summary="canary release r3.14 caused transient 5xx + noisy absolute alerts; mitigated by flag kill and rollback; observability gaps identified".
amelia: follow-up: schedule a short postmortem sync tomorrow 10am. invite owners: samir, jordan, nora, infra. I'll draft the page.
nora: logging note — we also found missing request identifiers in a subset of canary logs which made tracing harder. file: ops/logs/missing-request-id
oncall: closing the active paging loop. if anything else pops i'll reopen. tagging: :white_check_mark:
samir: thanks all. will post a concise incident summary to #incidents and link to the follow-up ticket.
jordan: team takeaway: treat canaries as tiny populations — alerts and dashboards must be population-aware. low blast radius doesn't mean low visibility.
amelia: filing tickets: ALERTS-204, DASH-117, RUNBOOK-58. will assign and track.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 = resolved -> monitoring. final state: rollback complete, customer impact minimal, follow-ups created.
